Executive Overview & Problem Statement ### The Problem On-demand food delivery platforms thrive on instant gratification but fail everyday working professionals who want a healthy, cost-effective lunch habit. Traditional subscriptions attempt to solve this, but suffer from **three structural failure points**: 1. **Decision Fatigue & Menu Monotony:** Users spend 20 minutes every morning picking lunch or get locked into repetitive, uninspiring single-kitchen menus. 2. **Hybrid Work Friction:** Inflexible delivery addresses force users to cancel or pause when switching between office days and Work-From-Home (WFH) days. 3. **Commitment Anxiety & Forfeited Meals:** Missing a single lunch because of sickness, sudden meetings, or dining out leads to churn when users lose money without rollover protection. ### The MealsOn Solution **MealsOn Scheduled Meals** transforms weekday lunch into a flexible, automated, and community-driven habit. Users pick an allowance tier and meal pass duration with built-in buffer validity days, auto-schedule menus via AI or their personal 20-item Food Vault, dynamically split deliveries across Office and Home, and enjoy 100% rollover protection on skipped meals. --- ## 🎯 2. Competitive Landscape & Market Positioning ### 6.1 The Competitive Dilemma: Why Prior Subscription Models Failed - **Local Tiffins & Dabbawalas:** Zero technology, single-kitchen monotony, cash-only, and completely inflexible when hybrid workers stay home. - **First-Gen App Subscriptions (Swiggy Daily):** Strict calendar locks. Users felt they wasted hard cash when 2–3 lunches were missed, triggering renewal churn. - **Diet Subscriptions (EatFit / Food Darzee):** Niche and expensive (₹300–₹450/meal) with rigid single-commissary menus leading to palate fatigue. - **Standard On-Demand (Swiggy / Zomato):** Excellent variety, but ₹45–₹65 in delivery and packaging fees per meal makes daily lunch ordering economically unviable. - **Zomato Everyday:** Solves homestyle affordability (₹150–₹180), but **remains purely on-demand**. Users still face daily decision fatigue, manual ordering, live 35-min wait times, and zero habit automation. ### 6.2 Comprehensive 5-Way Comparison Matrix
